root_cause_label: Agent implemented random synthetic data generation instead of matrix completion, ignoring observed entries as constraints
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent misunderstood the matrix completion task as random synthetic data generation, producing solution matrices that match only aggregate statistics (mean, std) while completely ignoring the observed sparse entries as constraints and the required low-rank structure.
t_err_evidence: Step 21: Agent creates generate_solutions.py using purely random row/col index sampling and normal-distribution value generation parameterized by aggregate statistics, with no reference to the provided observed_vals or the constraint that solution entries must match observed values at given (row, col) positions.
t_commit_evidence: Step 22: Agent executes generate_solutions.py and produces all 20 solution_{i}.txt files using the random generation approach; the incorrect outputs are now persisted on disk and all subsequent steps only verify aggregate statistics.
trigger_explanation: In step 7 the agent correctly identified 'matrix completion' as a possible approach but falsely assumed that generating random data matching aggregate statistics (mean, std) would satisfy the task, never recognizing that the observed triplets (row_idx, col_idx, observed_vals) are constraints that the output matrix must satisfy. The agent acted on the unverified assumption that statistical mimicry equals matrix completion.
fabrication_evidence: Step 22: All 20 solution files are generated as 200x200 matrices filled with random values drawn from normal distributions parameterized by aggregate statistics. The solutions do not honor the observed entries (the sparse matrix constraint) and are not derived from any form of matrix completion or low-rank reconstruction. The agent's verification in step 28 only checks that aggregate statistics (mean, std) match, confirming the fabrication was never detected.
